findings.summary: Replacement windows installed are vinyl units with simulated grilles rather than wood windows replicating original profiles required by NPS approval conditions.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-02 Condition 2 and DOC-07 Section 08 52 00 require replacement windows to replicate original wood profiles with true divided lites; DOC-14 quotes 412 white vinyl double-hung windows with simulated grilles between the glass, and DOC-15 confirms all windows were installed.
citations: DOC-02 p.3, Condition 2: 'Replacement windows must replicate the original wood profiles in material, dimensions and muntin pattern.'
DOC-07 p.6, 1: 'Wood windows replicating original profiles, with true divided lites matching the historic muntin pattern and profile.'
DOC-14 p.1, Item 1: 'Item 1 - Vinyl double-hung, standard profile'
DOC-14 p.1: 'Units are white vinyl with a standard sash profile and simulated grilles between the glass.'
DOC-15 p.4: 'Windows installed on floors 1 to 3.'
DOC-15 p.7: 'Windows on floors 4 and 5 are in.'
findings.explanation: Installing vinyl windows with simulated grilles directly violates NPS Part 2 Condition 2, jeopardizing Part 3 certification of completed work under 36 CFR 67.6 and the entire federal tax credit. The NPS approval conditions in DOC-02 govern over contractor purchase orders.

findings.summary: The federal historic tax credit in the financial model is calculated incorrectly as $5,120,000 instead of 20% of $24,600,000 of qualified expenditures.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-05 line 2.3 states the federal credit is $5,120,000 based on $24,600,000 of QRE; DOC-06 line 5 and DOC-11 Section 4.1(a) state the 20% federal credit on $24,600,000 is [text lost in copy]
citations: [text lost in copy] in thousands)'
DOC-05 p.2, 2.2: 'Federal historic tax credit rate: 20%'
DOC-05 p.2, 2.3: 'Federal historic tax credit: $5,120,000'
DOC-06 p.3, 4: 'Total qualified rehabilitation expenditures: $24,600,000'
DOC-06 p.3, 5: 'Federal rehabilitation credit: $4,920,000'
DOC-11 p.13, Section 4.1(a): 'The capital contribution has been calculated on projected federal credits of $4,920,000 at $0.88 per credit dollar.'
findings.explanation: Twenty percent of $24,600,000 is $4,920,000, not $5,120,000, creating an internal calculation error in DOC-05 of $200,000. The CPA cost certification draft DOC-06 and Operating Agreement DOC-11 govern over the financial model summary.

findings.summary: Federal investor equity in the financial model is overstated at $4,505,600 due to the erroneous credit amount rather than the agreed $4,329,600.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-05 line 2.5 calculates federal investor equity as $4,505,600; DOC-04 line 4 and DOC-11 Section 4.1 establish total federal equity at [text lost in copy]
citations: [text lost in copy] in thousands)'
DOC-04 p.1, line 4: 'Federal historic tax credit equity $4,329,600'
DOC-11 p.13, Section 4.1: 'The Investor Member shall contribute a total of $4,329,600 to the capital of the Company, payable in installments as set out in Section 4.2.'
findings.explanation: The financial model multiplies the incorrect $5,120,000 credit by $0.88 to arrive at $4,505,600, whereas 20% of [text lost in copy] 4,920,000) at $0.88 equals $4,329,600. The signed Operating Agreement DOC-11 and development budget DOC-04 govern over the model summary.

findings.summary: The capital contribution installment schedule in Section 4.2 sums to $4,429,600, exceeding the total agreed contribution of $4,329,600 in Section 4.1 by $100,000.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-11 Section 4.1 sets total capital contribution at $4,329,600; DOC-11 Section 4.2 lists installments of $865,920, $1,298,880, $1,831,840, and $432,960 that total $4,429,600.
citations: DOC-11 p.13, Section 4.1: 'The Investor Member shall contribute a total of [text lost in copy] 865,920, being 20% of the capital contribution'
DOC-11 p.14, Section 4.2(b): '[text lost in copy] 1,831,840, being 40% upon receipt of Part 3 approval from the National Park Service.'
DOC-11 p.14, Section 4.2(d): '$432,960, being 10% of the capital contribution'
findings.explanation: Forty percent of $4,329,600 is $1,731,840, but Section 4.2(c) incorrectly states $1,831,840, creating a $100,000 internal contradiction within the Operating Agreement. Section 4.1 defining total contribution should govern.

findings.summary: The development budget includes non-qualifying parking lot and FF&E expenditures in its total qualified rehabilitation costs.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-04 lines 31, 34, and 38 classify $420,000 of parking lot costs and $290,000 of furniture, fixtures and equipment as qualified; DOC-06 Section 1 explicitly excludes parking and furniture from qualified expenditures.
citations: DOC-04 p.2, line 31: 'Parking lot Yes $420,000'
DOC-04 p.2, line 34: 'Furniture, fixtures and equipment Yes $290,000'
DOC-04 p.2, line 38: 'Total qualified costs $25,310,000 $25,310,000'
DOC-06 p.3, 1: 'Costs for acquisition, land, site work outside the building, parking and furniture are excluded.'
findings.explanation: Under IRC Section 47(c)(2) and Treas. Reg. Section 1.48-12(c)(5), parking lots, site improvements, and personal property such as furniture and fixtures are statutory exclusions from QREs. The CPA cost certification draft DOC-06 correctly excludes these items and governs over the developer estimate DOC-04.

findings.claims_compared: DOC-12 Section 2.1 establishes a signed sale price of [text lost in copy] 5,043,000 proceeds in DOC-04); DOC-13 Section 2.1, DOC-05 line 2.6, and DOC-16 item 3 claim pricing of [text lost in copy] 5,227,500 proceeds).
citations: DOC-12 p.3, Section 2.1: 'Price. Buyer shall pay $0.82 per $1.00 of credit for all Credits transferred at Closing.'
DOC-04 p.1, line 5: 'Virginia historic tax credit proceeds $5,043,000'
DOC-13 p.3, Section 2.1: 'Price. Buyer shall pay $0.85 per $1.00 of credit for all Credits transferred at Closing.'
DOC-05 p.2, 2.6: 'Virginia credit price per credit dollar: 0.85'
DOC-16 p.1, 3: 'Virginia credits sold at $0.85 per credit.'
findings.explanation: The executed purchase agreement DOC-12 dated November 4, 2024 is legally binding and governs over the unexecuted draft DOC-13, financial model DOC-05, and investor memo DOC-16. Relying on $0.85 overstates state credit proceeds by [text lost in copy]

citations: DOC-05 p.4, 4.1: 'Federal credits delivered: 2025 5,120; 2026 to 2029 0 ($ in thousands)'

findings.summary: Total budgeted developer fee of $2,750,000 exceeds the $2,500,000 contractual fee cap in the Operating Agreement.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-04 lines 22 and 40 budget a developer fee of $2,750,000; DOC-11 Section 6.3 limits the developer fee to a maximum of $2,500,000 without prior written investor consent.
citations: DOC-04 p.1, line 22: 'Developer fee $2,750,000'
DOC-04 p.2, line 40: 'Developer fee (not included above) $2,750,000'
DOC-11 p.18, Section 6.3: 'The total development fee shall not exceed $2,500,000 without the prior written consent of the Investor Member.'
findings.explanation: The development budget includes a developer fee that is $250,000 higher than allowed by the governing partnership agreement. The Operating Agreement DOC-11 governs over the developer budget DOC-04.

findings.summary: The Operating Agreement text sets the recapture guaranty cap at $1,500,000, while the attached Form of Guaranty caps liability at $1,000,000.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-11 Section 7.4 states the credit recapture guaranty maximum is $1,500,000; DOC-11 Exhibit C paragraph 2 limits the Guarantor total liability for recapture to $1,000,000.
citations: DOC-11 p.21, Section 7.4: 'up to a maximum of $1,500,000.'
DOC-11 p.42, 2: 'The total liability of the Guarantor for recapture under this Guaranty shall not exceed $1,000,000.'
findings.explanation: The body of the agreement and Exhibit C provide conflicting caps on the guarantor exposure for tax credit recapture, creating a $500,000 discrepancy in investor indemnification protection.

findings.summary: Developer updates disclose a planned sale of commercial unit C-1 during the compliance period, contradicting transfer restrictions and the investor summary memo.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-15 Update, Oct 2025 plans to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective on June 30, 2026; DOC-11 Section 8.2 prohibits any unit sale during the 5-year compliance period without investor consent, and DOC-16 item 7 claims no sale or transfer is planned.
citations: DOC-15 p.12: 'We plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective, targeting June 30, 2026.'
DOC-11 p.24, Section 8.2: 'No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent'
DOC-16 p.2, 7: 'No sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned during the credit period.'
findings.explanation: Selling a portion of the building during the 5-year compliance period triggers partial recapture of the federal tax credit under IRC Section 50(a) and breaches Section 8.2 of the Operating Agreement.

findings.summary: The cost certification draft reflects only the base construction contract of $21,900,000 and omits $640,000 of executed change orders.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-06 line 3 lists the construction contract at $21,900,000; DOC-04 line 16 and DOC-08 Exhibit D show the adjusted contract sum is $22,540,000 following $640,000 in approved change orders.
citations: DOC-06 p.2, 3: 'Construction contract $21,900,000'
DOC-04 p.1, line 16: 'Hard construction (contract plus change orders) $22,540,000'
DOC-08 p.9: 'Adjusted contract sum after change orders $22,540,000'
findings.explanation: The CPA draft fails to reflect the executed change orders in the hard construction line item, reallocating $640,000 to qualified developer fee instead. The executed general contractor agreement and change orders DOC-08 govern.

findings.summary: The appraisal report evaluates 86 residential units, whereas architectural specifications, market study, and Part 2 specify 84 units.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-10 paragraph 1 describes proposed improvements as 86 units of rental housing; DOC-02 paragraph 1, DOC-03 paragraph 2, and DOC-07 paragraph 1 state the project contains 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.
citations: DOC-10 p.2, 1: 'Proposed improvements: 86 units of rental housing in a converted five-story mill'
DOC-02 p.2, 1: 'apartments on floors 1 to 5 and two commercial suites on the ground floor.'
DOC-03 p.1, 2: 'The subject will contain 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.'
DOC-07 p.1, 1: 'converts the former Ashby Mill into 84 apartments and 2 ground-floor commercial suites'
findings.explanation: The appraiser evaluated an 86-unit residential scheme, conflicting with the 84 residential units approved in architectural specifications and Part 2. The architect scope of work DOC-07 governs actual physical improvements.

findings.summary: The general construction agreement is dated June 5, 2023, but purports to incorporate architectural specifications dated July 20, 2023 and the Part 2 approval dated August 22, 2023.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-08 paragraphs 3 and 4 state the agreement was entered into June 5, 2023 and incorporates drawings dated July 20, 2023 and the approved Part 2; DOC-07 is dated July 20, 2023 and DOC-02 approval was issued August 22, 2023.
citations: DOC-08 p.1, 3: 'The Contract Documents include the drawings and specifications issued by Hollins and Reade Architects dated July 20, 2023, and the approved Part 2 application.'
DOC-08 p.1, 4: 'This Agreement is entered into as of June 5, 2023.'
DOC-07 p.1: 'ISSUE: JULY 20, 2023'
DOC-02 p.1: 'August 22, 2023'
findings.explanation: The contract was signed before the architectural specifications and Part 2 approval existed, creating contractual ambiguity as to what documents were bound on June 5, 2023.

findings.summary: The equity bridge loan matures on March 31, 2026, but the financial model projects receipt of the third equity installment on June 30, 2026.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-04 lines 9-10 state the bridge loan matures on March 31, 2026 and is repaid from installment 3; DOC-05 paragraph 4.3 projects installment 3 will be received on June 30, 2026.
citations: DOC-04 p.1, line 9: 'Equity bridge loan $1,700,000, matures 3/31/2026 (memo)'
DOC-04 p.1, line 10: 'Interim only; repaid from federal equity installment 3'
DOC-05 p.4, 4.3: 'Installment 3 received June 30, 2026'
findings.explanation: The project faces a three-month liquidity gap and default on the bridge loan unless an extension is secured, since the dedicated repayment source arrives after maturity.

findings.summary: The state credit purchase agreement permits buyer termination if DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026, but the financial model projects receipt on July 31, 2026.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-12 Section 5.3 allows buyer to terminate and receive a refund if DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026; DOC-05 paragraph 4.4 projects proceeds received July 31, 2026.
citations: DOC-12 p.6, Section 5.3: 'If the DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026, Buyer may terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of the deposit.'
DOC-05 p.4, 4.4: 'Virginia credit proceeds received July 31, 2026'
findings.explanation: The financial model projects receipt of proceeds three months past the outside delivery date in the signed contract, exposing the project to cancellation and loss of the credit buyer.

findings.summary: Developer email claims NPS approved Part 3 in October 2025, but no official Part 3 certification letter exists in the data room.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-15 Email, Nov 3, 2025 asserts NPS approved Part 3 in October; no supporting NPS Part 3 approval document is in the data room.
citations: DOC-15 p.11: 'Quick note: NPS approved Part 3 in October. We will send the paperwork once we have it in hand and request the third installment.'
DOC-09 p.2, line 16: 'Part 3 submitted 9/30/2025'
findings.explanation: The claim rests solely on an informal developer update with no official NPS certification documentation, creating high risk given the unauthorized vinyl window installation.

findings.summary: The investor summary memo asserts Virginia DHR has issued final certification, but no DHR certification letter is present in the data room.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-16 paragraph 6 states Virginia DHR has issued final certification for the state credits; no DHR certification document is provided in the data room.
citations: DOC-16 p.2, 6: 'Virginia DHR has issued final certification for the state credits.'
DOC-12 p.2, Section 1.2: 'DHR Certification means the final certification of the Credits issued by the Virginia Department of Historic Resources.'
findings.explanation: State credit monetization under DOC-12 is contingent upon DHR final certification, which cannot be verified without the official state certification document.

findings.summary: The as-is appraised value figure on page 4 of the appraisal excerpt is blurred and completely illegible.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-10 page 4 paragraph 1 contains blurred, illegible text for the value of the building.
citations: DOC-10 p.4, 1: '[Illegible blurred text under Value of the building]'
findings.explanation: The lender starting point for loan-to-value calculations cannot be verified from the data room because the text has been blurred out.

findings.summary: Developer updates claim the building was placed in service on March 28, 2025 upon Phase 1 TCO, while the cost certification and schedule report July 15, 2025.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-15 Update, Apr 2025 states the building was placed in service March 28 with Phase 1 TCO; DOC-06 paragraph 2 and DOC-09 milestone 14 report placed in service as July 15, 2025.
citations: DOC-15 p.8: 'Building placed in service March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO. Residents have started moving in on floors 1 to 3.'
DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'The building was placed in service on July 15, 2025'
DOC-09 p.2, line 14: 'Placed in service 7/15/2025'
findings.explanation: Partial occupancy of lower floors in March 2025 could constitute placing those units in service for tax purposes under Treas. Reg. Section 1.48-12(f)(2). The certified CPA report DOC-06 governs the project-wide placed-in-service date.

findings.summary: The development budget sources and uses shows an unfunded deficit gap of $600,000 despite including $600,000 of deferred developer fee.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-04 lines 12, 24, and 25 show total uses of $31,750,000 against total sources of [text lost in copy] 600,000).
citations: DOC-04 p.1, line 7: 'Deferred developer fee $600,000'
DOC-04 p.1, line 12: 'Total sources $31,150,000'
DOC-04 p.1, line 24: 'Total uses $31,750,000 [text lost in copy] 600,000) ($600,000)'
findings.explanation: The development budget does not balance and reveals an unfinanced $600,000 gap that threatens project completion unless additional capital is sourced.

findings.summary: The financial model assumes an aggressive lease-up pace of 12 units per month, contradicting the market study projection of 7 units per month.
findings.claims_compared: DOC-03 paragraph 4 projects absorption of 7 units per month and warns against faster assumptions; DOC-05 paragraph 3.2 assumes 12 units per month.
citations: DOC-03 p.8, 4: 'We project an absorption pace of 7 units per month; stabilization in about 12 months, defined as 93% physical occupancy.'
DOC-03 p.8, 5: 'A faster pace would require pricing below the proposed rents and is not assumed.'
DOC-05 p.3, 3.2: 'Lease-up assumption: 12 units per month from the first unit delivered.'
findings.explanation: Overstating the absorption pace by over 70% distorts working capital, operating deficit reserves, and permanent loan conversion timing. The independent market study DOC-03 governs realistic market absorption.

findings.claims_compared: DOC-07 page 1 header names the owner as Ashbey Mill Owner LLC; DOC-01 paragraph 1, DOC-08 paragraph 1, and DOC-11 Preamble name the owner as Ashby Mill Owner LLC.
citations: DOC-07 p.1: 'OWNER: Ashbey Mill Owner LLC'
DOC-01 p.1, 1: 'Owner of record: Ashby Mill Owner LLC, a Virginia limited liability company.'
DOC-08 p.1, 1: 'Between Ashby Mill Owner LLC (Owner) and Blue Ridge Builders Inc.'
